Russell Lebo / Selected Works2008-2026

Design for a more just, informed, and engaged human experience

I am an experience designer, creative technologist, and occasional anthropologist

It’s true. I work with teams developing digital products or services across healthcare, civic tech, human rights, museums, cultural institutions, global brands, and education.

My role is to provide human-centered design direction and strategy. I find the insights into real human behavior that guide a team’s design decisions. I develop prototypes to test and validate those decisions when they are still cheap to make.

The Minimum Testable Product

I like to test designs early and often. For me, the ideal development strategy is not about finding the shortest route to MVP. It is about finding the shortest route to insight.

I call this approach the Minimum Testable Product. Instead of advancing in fits and starts, design and development are always moving forward. It is a process of continuous improvement.

Equitable Access to Insight

I have always been interested in the ways people turn information into knowledge. One of the best tools we have for this is information visualization, infovis for short. The problem is that for the visually impaired, infovis is not going to help. For them, that knowledge remains locked away in the data.

To figure this out, I have been exploring sonification - the presentation of data as sound. It is not a new concept, but there is surprisingly little happening in the field. That’s why I’ll be writing about this over the coming weeks. Maybe we can figure it out together.

Impact

From my first job as an interaction designer to leading design for $60M federal contracts and making decisions that impact 300 million people, I have been extraordinarily lucky to work alongside people, organizations, and institutions looking to improve lives.

  • IBM Interactive

    Smart Decisions, Smart Cities

    CityForward was an innovative web platform developed by IBM as part of its Smarter Planet Initiative. Designed to serve city officials, researchers, academics, and engaged citizens, CityForward offered a comprehensive view of urban life across 250 major cities globally. The platform aimed to facilitate data-driven decision-making and foster a deeper understanding of urban trends.

  • ICA Boston, Bluecadet

    A Museum that Talks with its Visitors

    Bluecadet and the Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) Boston took an innovative approach to enhance visitor engagement and accessibility to the museum’s art collections through interactive kiosks. The project sought to transform the museum experience by integrating technology into the gallery-education space, enabling rich dialogues between the museum, its artists, and its visitors.
